claims.subject: mb_adi_later_kindama
claims.summary: Kīndama, in the form of a mating deer, is struck by Pāṇḍu’s arrows.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: The speaking deer identifies himself as Kīndama, a sage, at 1.109.26–27.

claims.subject: mb_adi_later_kindama
claims.summary: Kīndama curses Pāṇḍu to die if he approaches a wife in sexual union.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: The curse is the stated consequence of Pāṇḍu killing Kīndama and his mate while they are mating.

claims.subject: epic
claims.summary: Pāṇḍu cites Agastya’s sacrificial hunt as a precedent in his exchange with Kīndama.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: The passage says Agastya hunted forest animals during a sattra and offered the animals as sacrificial victims; it does not connect Agastya genealogically to either speaker.

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_pandu
claims.summary: Pāṇḍu addresses Kuntī and Mādrī as his wives before announcing his forest renunciation.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_pandu
claims.summary: Pāṇḍu addresses Kuntī and Mādrī as his wives before announcing his forest renunciation.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_pandu
claims.summary: Yudhiṣṭhira is called Pāṇḍu’s firstborn son and is included among Pāṇḍu’s sons.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: Dharma is named separately as Yudhiṣṭhira’s divine begetter.

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_pandu
claims.summary: Bhīma is included among Pāṇḍu’s sons; the narration also names Vāyu as his divine begetter.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_pandu
claims.summary: Arjuna is born to Kuntī through Indra and identified as one of Pāṇḍu’s sons.

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_pandu

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_pandu

claims.subject: mb_adi_inc_vayu

claims.subject: mb_adi_inc_ashvin_twins

claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: The twin deity pair is retained as a single pair node; it is not expanded into separately named gods.

claims.subject: mb_adi_inc_ashvin_twins
claims.summary: Mādrī invokes the Aśvin twins, who produce Sahadeva.

claims.subject: mb_adi_inc_bhimasena_human_incarnation

claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: This claim records only the shared birth date; it does not make Duryodhana Pāṇḍu’s son.

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_pandu

claims.subject: mb_adi_later_vyushitashva
claims.summary: After Vyuṣitāśva’s death, Bhadrā conceives three Śālva and four Madra sons through him.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: The sons are not named in this passage and are not modeled as individual people.

claims.subject: mb_adi_later_sharadvata

claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: The text explains the twins’ birth from Śaradvat’s semen after Jālapadī appears; it does not state that they were born from her body.

claims.subject: mb_adi_later_sharadvata

notes: This batch is limited to Ādiparvan 1.109–1.145, disjoint from the prior 1.95–1.108 batch and the other agent’s 1.62–1.88 span.

The named divine and sage assembly at Arjuna’s birth (1.114.40–63) is represented by individually named figures. Unnamed collectives such as the eight Vasus, Maruts, and additional Nāgas are excluded. Aśvin twins remain one deity-pair node.

Homonyms in the birth-assembly rosters use role-specific IDs (for example, the Gandharva Bhīmasena is not merged with the Pandava Bhīma; Gandharva Dhṛtarāṣṭra is not the Kuru king). The Apsaras Marīci is likewise separate from sage Marīci.

The five Pandava identities reuse existing Ādiparvan human-incarnation IDs; their divine begetters are separately modeled from Pāṇḍu’s dynastic fatherhood. The Aśvins are kept as a pair rather than two unnamed individual nodes.
No unnamed offspring or unlisted Kaurava names have been inflated into individual people. Repeated or ambiguous roster forms are not expanded beyond grammatical evidence.
